ParlaMint-AT_1996-07-11-020-XX-NRSITZ-00036_d7e5274	Federal Minister! ==References== Austria is a member of the EU. My question is: [[/PAKT/VHG/XX/M/M_00025/index.shtml -- 25/M]] What have been the consequences of the adoption of the EU external trade regime for Austrian foreign trade?
ParlaMint-AT_1996-07-11-020-XX-NRSITZ-00036_d7e5301	Federal Minister, please.
ParlaMint-AT_1996-07-11-020-XX-NRSITZ-00036_d7e5316	Deputies! Because of the basicity of your question, I would like to give a more detailed answer. First of all, we are dealing with the most important internal market countries. Although we do not have official statistics, we know from statistics from the EU Member States that there has actually been a marked increase in exports to the countries of the European Union, and it is particularly striking that the number of exporters has almost tripled. One can not only speak of exporters but rather of suppliers and stakeholders from the internal market. This is the practical development of the market. It seems to me far more important to consider – and this is the subject of your question – what legal or positional changes have occurred since accession. As regards trade with third countries, Austria had to adopt the EU quotas and the Community tariff. This led to a regime that, unfortunately, is more restrictive than that previously handled in Austria. On the other hand, it helps us, in cooperation with liberal participating countries in the European Union, to push for an overall more liberal EU foreign trade regime. The position of Austria vis-à-vis EU third countries was not fully affected insofar as most of the quotas could be taken over accordingly. Trade with other important partner countries of Austria in Central and Eastern Europe has resulted from the adoption of the EU regime. These exist, in particular, in the absence of known discriminations in passive processing, which has almost quadrupled since accession, thanks to the removal of these difficulties. Trade with the free trade partners Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Poland, Romania and Bulgaria is particularly favourable. Another important point is that with the accession, we have received greater potential for influence in the WTO, the World Trade Organisation. If we take our weight in the WTO before accession, with about 1 per cent of the world's share of trade, it was extremely small. Especially since our membership, we have been participants in the so-called quarter, in this four-group EU, Canada and USA or developing countries, where we are actually obese in a group compared to what happened before. I would like to point out that I had the experience of not knowing in part what the quarter had been discussing in the preliminary phase of important GATT negotiations. . So we have practically become bigger in the integration of world trade issues through accession, perhaps to say something plausible. As far as other bilateral negotiations are concerned, we can say that our weight has certainly increased by membership of the EU. I also recall the EU's negotiations with the Maghreb-Mashhad countries. So far, we have at best been confronted with facts in the EFTA and EEA frameworks – now we can de facto co-negotiate. A very important point seems to me to be that there are incredible opportunities for small and medium-sized enterprises in particular to establish themselves in this single market in the longer term.

I report on the Government template (198 of the supplements): The Federal Act amending the 1992 AMA Act. The second section of the AMA Act contains a scheme for the application of contributions to the promotion of agricultural marketing in the fruit and vegetable sector. The current government proposal was adopted by the Committee on Agriculture and Forestry at its meeting on 2 October. Negotiating on 1 July 1996. The Members of Parliament Georg Schwarzenberger, Heinz Gradwelt and Comrades tabled an extensive amendment. In the vote, the Government template was adopted by a majority vote in the version of the amendment mentioned above. As a result of its deliberations, the Committee on Agriculture and Forestry makes the request that the National Council give the draft Constitutional consent to the draft legislation annexed to the written report. I also report on the Government template (199 of the Supplements): Federal Law on the Traffic of Vines. The current grape transport law dates back to 1948 and no longer meets the requirements of the European Community in a wide range of areas. With Austria's accession to the European Union, it is necessary to take into account in detail the legislation currently in force in the Community on the propagation of vines. The current government proposal was adopted by the Committee on Agriculture and Forestry at its meeting on 2 October. Negotiating on 1 July 1996. In the vote, the current government proposal was adopted by a majority vote. As a result of its deliberations, the Committee on Agriculture and Forestry therefore proposes that the National Council should give the draft law submitted by the Federal Government a constitutional agreement. I also report on the Government template (200 of the supplements): The Federal Law on Forest Propagation and Federal Law amending the Forest Law 1975. Forests in their biological and genetic diversity represent an irreplaceable heritage. To preserve this diversity, the conservation of genetic resources is also essential. In order to ensure the genetic adaptability of forest resources, it is therefore necessary to avoid the use of reproductive material which, by virtue of its genetic characteristics, can exert an adverse influence. MEPs Georg Schwarzenberger, Heinz Gradwelt and Comrades tabled an amendment. At the time of the vote, the Government template was partially adopted unanimously, partly by majority, in the text of the amendment tabled by Georg Schwarzenberger, Heinz Gradwelt and Comrades. As a result of its deliberations, the Committee on Agriculture and Forestry therefore proposes that the National Council give constitutional approval to the draft law submitted by the Federal Government with the amendments to the written committee report. I also report on the Government template (156 of the Supplements): Protocol amending the European Convention on the Protection of Animals in Agricultural Animals. The European Convention on the Protection of Animals in Agricultural Animals was given in Austria before the ratification of the parliamentary approval as a legislative amendment and a legislative supplement to the State Treaty. The Committee on Agriculture and Forestry took note of the government's current proposal at its meeting on 2 October. Negotiating on 1 July 1996. At the time of the vote, it was unanimously decided to recommend to the National Council the approval of the conclusion of this Protocol. As a result of its opinion, the Committee on Agriculture and Forestry therefore proposes that the National Council: The conclusion of the State Treaty: Protocol amending the European Convention on the Protection of Animals in Agricultural Animals (156 of the Supplements) is hereby approved. ParlaMint-AT_1996-07-11-020-XX-NRSITZ-00036_d7e18249	Mr President. Federal Minister! Ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen! The second speech by Mr Reichhold has prompted me to speak once again, in order to clarify something here. The former system of our agricultural prices, i.e. the political influence on agricultural prices by export support, has been repeatedly criticized by the opposition with the justification that the exporters will be encouraged and our products thrown away on the world market. Again and again the demand was made to give farmers the means previously spent on export support directly in the form of land premiums. In the course of the common agricultural policy in the European Union from 1992 onwards, pricing has been converted into this system with a view to the previous GATT negotiations. It is, of course, depressing for a farmer and a psychological burden if prices fall within a year, almost half of cereals, where milk reaches a third, by 20 to 25 percent in the meat, even though this could be largely offset by subsidies. That is why it was so important in the negotiations for Austria to first set the corresponding quotas, wherever there are market regulations. With the exception of the sugar sector, we have succeeded in securing existing production in Austria, which we would not have been allowed by the GATT agreements to and for ourselves, because we should have reduced subsidies by 36 percent and the quantity by 21 percent. Nevertheless, the European Treaty has resulted in a reduction in income or prices in different areas. On the one hand, a storage charge is paid for those goods which were produced at high prices and with expensive means of operation in 1994, but from 1 January 1994 onwards. As a result of the internal market, there was a corresponding fall in prices in January 1995. The second area: In the course of the negotiations, accession compensatory contributions were always considered. However, this has not been tolerated by the European Union, and we had to accept the single market with accession immediately. As a compensation, the European Union has offered us appropriate funding from the European Union as a degressive contribution, which in the first year, i.e. last year, amounted to about 7.2 billion schillings and will be around 4.5 billion shillings in this year, in order to achieve this price shock. Then to another area, namely structural assistance. Since the European Union has a much different classification system for mountain areas – there is the local classification, while there is a single-company classification in Austria – our mining classification had to be changed to the new EU classification. As a result, 40 000 farmers and farmers in disadvantaged regions now have more than before accession to the EU. 2 200 farms, which were classified as mining establishments before accession to the EU, but now no longer, are now receiving ten years of the mining aid they received in 1993. This is secured. Nevertheless, we want to try to classify a substantial part of mining plants by fine-tuning and re-adjustment as farms in disadvantaged regions. This should reduce market distortions and restrictions on competition. Access to energy technology is encouraged. Ladies and gentlemen! The Parties undertake to comply with international environmental conventions to minimise environmental hazards. They are committed, and I think this is particularly important, to the polluter principle and the other to improve energy efficiency. The environmental focus is highlighted in particular in the Energy Efficiency Protocol. This largely corresponds to the orientation of our energy policy. Austrian government policy aims to involve the reform states of Central and Eastern Europe and the CIS countries in international economic and environmental cooperation. Many good reasons speak for this. This objective, we believe, is largely in line with the Energy Charter and the Protocol. We shall therefore vote in favour of this Energy Charter. ParlaMint-AT_1996-07-11-020-XX-NRSITZ-00036_d7e25944	Mr President. Federal Minister! Dear ladies and gentlemen! Mr. Haigermoser! Dr. Graf: This is flexibility!]] Even if the liberals do not agree with the amendment of the customs law implementing law, I would like to comment briefly from the point of view of the coalition on this customs law enforcement law, because the text we are today discussing on the decision-making of the amendment of the customs law implementing the law must be seen in the context of the creation of the border service in the Federal Army and also with the new border control law. Ladies and gentlemen! On its own, the amendment of the Customs Enforcement Act would seem to the effect that the customs administration would largely refrain from having customs law implemented by its institutions itself. However, when considering both laws relating to the border control law, it is recognized that these are merely a counterpart to the involvement of the customs authorities in the implementation of border control. Both laws together are, therefore, an essential contribution to taking account of the demand for economy in the administration. Customs authorities should carry out border controls where, due to the traffic situation, it is appropriate to carry out border controls as bodies of the security authorities, and on the other hand, public security authorities should carry out tasks of the customs administration to a different extent in other border crossings. Both laws do not mean that one of the two administrative areas replaces or displaces the other. It is not the case that customs bodies carry out such checks on customs and foreign law, nor that security bodies as such take care of cross-border trade in goods, but that each institution of one administration is involved in the execution of the other administration. The concept of both laws therefore seems appropriate to me, since both together prevent the need to provide services to smaller cross-border bodies from two areas of administration, so that they can be carried out at any border crossing of the staff which allows for simple, economical and yet effective enforcement of the laws. The second point, the amendment of the Mineral Oil Tax Act, which also amends the alcohol – tax and monopoly law – and I think that it is necessary to say that too – to alter the excise administration of consumption, or to remove it from the Ministry of Finance. Reasons for this: With the integration of Austria into the European Union, of course, the so-called production monopoly for alcohol must also be liberalised. The change of law therefore provides for the domestic demand system to be extended by the federal government and the tasks transferred to the manufacturers themselves. In this context, financial resources for structural improvements in agriculture will also be considered useful by the year 2000 – and that is necessary – in degressive allocation. The dangers of wild streams, avalanches and erosions are constantly present not only in the narrowest living and economic sectors, but also in the agricultural and forestry areas, as well as, of course, in the area of binding transport routes and tourist facilities. Recent storms and related damage are a lasting proof of the importance of this facility. Of particular importance, however, is also the preparation of the so-called hazard zone plans, which primarily benefit the spatial planning and, more generally, also the construction authority as an assessment aid for the release of endangered areas. The forestry service is currently planned for 900 projects in Austria with an approved construction volume of 4 billion Schilling. The annual effort for the implementation of the projects is on average 1.4 billion schilling over the last three years. These measures are carried out 48 percent of the own construction of the Wildbach and avalanche plant, which currently has 1,620 employees, with the work operations referring to the most difficult specialist and site areas. It is precisely this construction that is in front of the financial collapse when federal funds are cut down. With all the love of privatization, I doubt that in this area of private enterprises in particular, it is cost-effective to be able to carry out the extensive support work. On the other hand, it is very likely that privatisation with regard to the construction of larger construction projects in this area will be possible, which has already been done for a long time in my knowledge. The allocation of the promised disaster fund is within the competence of the Minister of Agriculture, and as the necessary budgetary resources are provided, I would like to ask the critical question as to why the production of wildlife and avalanche is much lower. 1 620 workers now have to expect, through internal and budgetary cuts, the loss of their jobs or significantly longer periods of unemployment, especially in winter. We know that there can be no 100% protection against natural disasters. However, it must be tried to expand the protection, because prevention is better than repairing. Allow me a few more sentences on the constant requests of the liberals for the abolition of the drinking tax and, for some areas, also the municipal tax. It is not only that the financing of the municipalities is being called into question here that the change in the taxation of beverages in 1992 has shown us when the extra alcohol tax on excise duties has been changed and the drinking tax on non-alcoholic beverages has been halved and therefore the drinks in the hospitality sector have been taxed significantly, but paradoxically this has not been reflected in the prices of beverages in the future. [[Abg. Rossmann: That's what the Chamber of Commerce is doing!]] The consumer still has to pay the higher prices. I am thinking, above all, of non-alcoholic beverages. For example, if I produce the mineral water, where at a purchase price of 3 s about a litre, a sales price of over 60 s is required. It is obvious that there was no need for competition to pass on the tax advantages to consumers as well. Therefore: A replacement-free abolition of the levy would put most communities in real financial difficulties. Therefore, only a clear no can be given on the part of the municipal representatives to abolish the drinking tax without replacement.

A specific problem of the flow of purchasing power cannot therefore be the levy on beverages. The Austrians' tendency to take drinks with them on trips will hardly be eliminated by the withdrawal of the drinking tax because this is due to a general consumption behaviour of tourists. The administrative effort mentioned is also minimal. With regard to the unique nature of the drinking tax in Austria, I would like to mention that there are excise duties similar to those in the EU, such as in Germany, England, France and Italy. Any price differences between Austrian and foreign drinks can therefore in no way be solely due to the excise duty. For health reasons, but also for competition reasons, the alcohol tax was removed in 1992 under the new rules on the taxation of beverages and the rate of non-alcoholic beverages was reduced from 10 to 5 percent. In this context too, the Austrian municipal government has always made itself strongly committed to ensuring the location of local services. ==References== 1. This abolition would necessarily limit the order volume of the municipalities and thus undermine the financial security of the largest contracting authority. ParlaMint-AT_1996-07-11-020-XX-NRSITZ-00036_d7e26533	Mr President. Mr. Federal Minister! Ladies and gentlemen! We are now dealing, among other things, with a government template that amends the Banking Act. In my contribution to the debate, I would like to deal with the anonymous securities deposit, the so-called §-12 business. What is the current situation? – The customer goes to the bank to the investment advisor, and in a conversation the future charge will be discussed. It will be provided with money and an anonymous securities account will be opened. The account is provided with an account name and a ransom word is agreed, and the account holder receives a voucher or a juxte. Only with this bonus or juxte, which is of course transferable – that is a holder’s paper – can the respective account be held. What is the problem now? My venerations Ladies and gentlemen! The problem lies in the fact that, due to this anonymous possibility of investment in securities, we are being accused by foreign countries that these anonymous accounts could operate insider transactions or money laundering. Ladies and gentlemen! With the amendment of the Banking Act, the newly introduced § 40 is intended to prevent the suspicion that securities accounts will not be used as money laundering. In the future, for example, upon opening an securities account, the authorisation of the account holder is in any case necessary – whether foreigners or nationals – and the signature is to be given on the corresponding signature sheet. Of course, there are transitional arrangements, in the case of existing anonymous securities deposit accounts the sale or use of paper remains anonymous. The purpose of this transitional scheme is to avoid the sudden sale of securities and to allow anonymous investors to withdraw from anonymous investment. Ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen! Of course, the domestic banks have no pleasure in the complete abolition of anonymity in the securities business. They fear that this new regulation will lead to massive money outflows abroad. However, I would particularly like to point out that this measure does not affect our banking secrecy. In conclusion, I would like to stress that this change of law in the Banking Act sends a clear signal, a signal to gain confidence, especially in relation to foreign countries, and thus the attractiveness of our financial base. Vienna is being strengthened.

And that seems to me to be particularly important, because water cannot be handled carefully enough. There is no doubt that Austria has been a pioneer in this area and has put in place very important measures in the area of wastewater treatment and the introduction of wastewater into our rivers and lakes. Not for nothing we have a water quality goodness 2 and 2 to 3 in the Danube. But it would be of no use to us if Austria were to take the best measures if the neighbouring states did not, because a river and an ecosystem live on this good water quality, and not only the ecosystem, but also our people. The Danube is a guarantee for drinking water reserves not only the city of Vienna, but also many other larger neighbouring cities. In addition to the ecological need for pure groundwater, for pure rivers, the Danube also has a very important energy policy aspect in the field of transport routes. It all means a substantial savings when goods and goods are transported on a waterway. There is, however, a danger in terms of the introduction of the Danube, because especially in the remaining free flow routes, we have a huge depth of soles. But I am optimistic that all of this can be improved accordingly by means of an international agreement. Ladies and gentlemen, ladies and gentlemen! I think it is very useful that this agreement, which has been discussed for many years, can finally be decided in Austria, and I am pleased that it will be decided today. I expect the approval of everyone.

Another problem, which has also been criticized, is still open. This is the supply of the so-called high terrace. It is only slightly higher than the low terrace. According to the project, one should install pipelines and bring the water to the surfaces from these pipelines. At present, a new idea is being considered, whereby some believe that this will not be done, that you should also pour or rain on the high terrace, but that you must also bring in contaminants to enrich the groundwater and then extract the water from the groundwater. The Federal Government and the State of Lower Austria are currently working behind the scenes to reach agreement in intensive discussions on further operations or to raise funds for financing. In fact, 200 million shilling is still reserved for the high terrace and about 127 million shilling is available for operating costs. Finally, I would like to join the Court of Auditors only if he believes that, regardless of small criticisms, society has offered an ecologically balanced solution, that through contact with the population in planning and construction without disturbances it could work and fulfil its legal mandate. I believe that we can accept with good conscience the corresponding report on the Court of Auditors' report or the 1994 report.

Not the Ambulance Fund is the cause of increasing ambulance frequency, but the suction effect of high quality. In the early days, in the hospitals of the federal states, ambulances and benefits from the mother-child passport were made available to doctors as private money with the distribution key 40 to 60. I prefer an ambulance fund that is used for hospital needs. That's just like Mag. The Committee's main concern is that six percent private patients are in the AKH, due to the excellent medical and hotel services available to all patients. It is therefore more interesting for private patients to enjoy the daily rate as compensation, than to pay for a service provided free of charge by the State. However, if a patient is looking for a certain doctor, if the procedure makes it responsible, he would rather explain the patient in one of the private hospitals in the neighborhood of the AKH for pecuniary reasons. In the event of complications, the patient is transported immediately to the home of top medical care and provided there at the expense of the general public. With regard to the numerous private accounts of the clinics, I agree with the AKH report, which needs to be reduced and more manageable. Services provided by the public authorities may not be diverted to private accounts. I share the criticism of the re-purchasing of equipment during the transfer, but I would also like to praise the smooth, labour-intensive and rapid transfer. A research and teaching hospital must be at the very latest state of the art equipment, so the AKH will be able to exchange equipment more quickly than in other hospitals. A common personnel plan of the federal government and the municipality is desirable. The most suitable way to ensure optimal management of the university clinics would be to have a separate operating company for all three university clinics. Thus, unnecessary costs resulting from double-trackness could be avoided and – humanitarianly acceptable – the cost of economics could be taken into account. University clinics, as little as ministries, parliament, schools, police, fire brigades or the Court of Auditors, can work profitably or cost-neutral. The services provided are supposed to satisfy us with pride. Nevertheless, we must create the conditions for the proposed improvements. I hope all of us get to know this wonderful hospital only on visits. – I thank you for the patient listening or not listening and wish you all a nice summer!
